Title: A Beetle Like No Other
Content: A bug races near a stream. It dashes across a rock. Its long legs bend and stretch. Its bright blue body shines in the sun. Its large eyes pop out. It has wings, but it is not a fly. What is it?
Tiger beetles are insects. They are part of the beetle family. These beetles have long, brightly colored bodies that look like jewels. They can have a shiny blue, green, orange, or red color.

Tiger beetles are faster than other beetles. This is because of their long legs. They can run up to speeds of `text(five and a half miles per hour)`. How fast is that? To match the speed of a tiger beetle, a person would have to run `text(480 miles per)` hour. That's almost as fast as an airplane!

Speed helps tiger beetles catch food. Their large eyes also help. With their sharp vision, tiger beetles can spot a meal from far away. Then, they are off and running. But they move so fast that they lose sight of their meal. Tiger beetles must stop to focus. Now they can locate their food again. Time to eat!

Tiger beetles aren't just fast runners, they are good fliers too! This helps them easily avoid danger. Tiger beetles can also spray a liquid when they are in trouble. The liquid smells like bubblegum. Other animals do not like the sweet smell.
Tiger beetles are special little creatures.
